node_definition.done_when: Done when. New tests, each failing at the base revision: With the roster at cap minus reserve, a queued codex request and two queued local requests, one admission pass launches the codex request and not a local one. A codex dispatch held at the cores bound or the roster cap is queued, not refused. A local dispatch that falls back to codex on context fit and meets the cap is queued, and its output names the context-fit shortfall. A refused dispatch prints no created run id without a pointer. A local dispatch that passed the queueing pre-check but meets the bound at the later check in preparation is queued (D179). The local lane is admitted to the full cap with no named request waiting, and stopped at cap minus reserve with one waiting. A queued local review edited to codex keeps its reviewed run and launches into the reserve. A codex request under a budget hold stays queued with the hold named. The tests importing the admission package or reckon.crew.queue_admission add no failure against the base on all_debug, one arm at a time with at most -n 4 . The gate logs go under the run directory, and the landing record goes in docs/evidence/fragments/the-escape-lane-and-reviews-keep-pace/named-lane-queues.html . The queueing already exists for the local lane: the roster refusal is caught and the request queued behind two is_local gates in reckon/crew/dispatching/preparation.py , and a metered lane's budget hold already queues. This section widens those gates to every lane and adds no second queue path. That also makes the roster refusal's promise, "a request queued behind this cap launches then", true for every lane, which today it is only for the local one. Write paths: the dispatch preparation and admission modules this needs, and the new tests.
